subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Polynesian star compass was used by navigators in the central Pacific from roughly 1200 to 1800.
• The compass divided the horizon into four quadrants, each containing seven named directional points.
• Each point was named after a fish, seabird, shell, or reef feature as a way of honoring an aspect of ocean life.
• Ko'olau is the northeastern quadrant of the compass.
• The fourth point of Ko'olau is named Manu, which means "seabird."
prompt: The student wants to emphasize how the Polynesian star compass honored ocean life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Each point in the Polynesian star compass was given a name honoring an aspect of ocean life; for example, a point in Ko'olau was named for a seabird.
choices.B: The northeastern quadrant of the Polynesian star compass, Ko'olau, contained seven named directional points.
choices.C: Each point in the Polynesian star compass was given a unique name; the fourth point of Ko'olau was no exception.
choices.D: Each point in the Polynesian star compass's quadrant of Ko'olau had a unique name.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes how the Polynesian star compass honored ocean life by stating that each point was given a name honoring an aspect of ocean life and by providing a specific example: a point in Ko'olau named for a seabird.
